target: Setiap tujuh belas Agustus, kampung kami mengadakan berbagai lomba untuk anak-anak dan orang dewasa.
english: Every seventeenth of August, our neighborhood holds various competitions for children and adults.
grammar: Independence Day is 17 Agustus; the whole festive season is called tujuh belasan.

target: Adik saya menang lomba makan kerupuk di lapangan dekat rumah kemarin sore.
english: My younger sibling won the cracker-eating contest at the field near the house yesterday afternoon.
grammar: Lomba makan kerupuk: eat a cracker hung on a string, hands behind your back — the classic race.

target: Bapak-bapak berusaha memanjat pohon pinang yang licin untuk mengambil hadiah di puncaknya.
english: The men try to climb the slippery areca-palm trunk to grab the prizes at its top.
grammar: Panjat pinang: teams climb a greased palm trunk for prizes tied at the top.

target: Anak-anak melompat dalam karung sampai garis akhir, dan penonton tertawa keras.
english: The children jump along in sacks to the finish line, and the spectators laugh loudly.

target: Sebelum lomba dimulai, kami mengikuti upacara bendera di lapangan kecamatan.
english: Before the races begin, we take part in the flag ceremony at the district field.

target: Warga kompleks bekerja sama memasang bendera merah putih di depan setiap rumah.
english: The residents of the complex work together putting up red-and-white flags in front of every house.

target: Ibu-ibu menghias gapura kampung dengan cat merah dan putih minggu lalu.
english: The neighborhood women decorated the kampung gateway with red and white paint last week.

target: Ayah dan paman ikut lomba tarik tambang melawan tim kampung sebelah.
english: Dad and my uncle join the tug-of-war against the team from the next kampung.

target: Tim ibu-ibu kalah tipis dalam lomba bakiak tahun ini.
english: The mothers' team lost narrowly in the wooden-clog race this year.

target: Hadiah utama lomba tahun ini sepeda baru dari pak lurah.
english: This year's main competition prize is a new bicycle from the village head.

target: Setelah upacara, ayah mengajak kami menonton pawai budaya di alun-alun.
english: After the ceremony, Dad takes us to watch the cultural parade on the town square.

target: Anak saya membawa bendera kecil dan mengikuti karnaval sekolah dengan bangga.
english: My child carries a small flag and joins the school carnival proudly.

target: Malam sebelum tujuh belas Agustus, warga berkumpul untuk malam tirakatan di balai kampung.
english: The night before August seventeenth, residents gather for the tirakatan evening at the kampung hall.
grammar: Malam tirakatan: neighbors gather on the eve of the 17th for prayers, speeches, and snacks.

target: Kakek bercerita tentang masa perjuangan setiap kali melihat upacara di televisi.
english: Grandpa tells stories about the independence struggle every time he sees the ceremony on television.

target: Panitia lomba membagikan hadiah kepada para pemenang sore harinya.
english: The competition committee hands out prizes to the winners that afternoon.

target: Suasana kampung meriah sekali dengan umbul-umbul warna-warni di sepanjang jalan.
english: The kampung atmosphere is very festive with colorful banners all along the road.

target: Kami sekeluarga memakai baju merah putih saat acara tujuh belasan di kompleks.
english: Our whole family wears red-and-white clothes during the Independence Day event at the complex.

target: Ibu tertawa melihat adik gagal memasukkan pensil ke dalam botol.
english: Mom laughs watching my little sibling fail to get the pencil into the bottle.

target: Ayah menjadi juri lomba paduan suara antarwarga tahun ini.
english: Dad is a judge for the inter-neighborhood choir competition this year.

target: Setelah semua lomba selesai, warga makan bersama di halaman masjid.
english: After all the competitions are over, residents eat together in the mosque courtyard.

target: Spanduk bertuliskan Dirgahayu Republik Indonesia digantung di depan kantor kelurahan.
english: A banner reading 'Long Live the Republic of Indonesia' is hung in front of the ward office.
grammar: Dirgahayu = 'long live', banner language: Dirgahayu Republik Indonesia.

target: Nenek paling suka menonton lomba balap karung dari teras rumahnya.
english: Grandma likes watching the sack race most, from the terrace of her house.

target: Tahun depan giliran kampung kami mengatur seluruh acara tujuh belasan.
english: Next year it is our kampung's turn to organize the whole Independence Day program.

target: Selama bulan Ramadan, banyak warung tutup pada siang hari.
english: During the month of Ramadan, many food stalls are closed in the daytime.

target: Teman kantor saya bangun jam tiga pagi untuk makan sahur.
english: My office friend gets up at three in the morning to eat the pre-dawn meal.
grammar: Sahur = the pre-dawn meal before a fasting day; the set phrase is makan sahur.

target: Ibu membangunkan seluruh keluarga untuk sahur sebelum imsak.
english: Mom wakes the whole family for the pre-dawn meal before the imsak cut-off.
grammar: Imsak = the cut-off a few minutes before dawn prayer — stop eating then.

target: Banyak orang menunggu waktu buka puasa sambil jalan-jalan sore, namanya ngabuburit.
english: Many people wait for the fast-breaking time while strolling in the afternoon; it's called ngabuburit.
grammar: Ngabuburit (Sundanese) = pleasantly killing time before buka puasa: strolling, hunting snacks.

target: Kami berbuka puasa dengan kurma dan es buah di rumah nenek.
english: We break the fast with dates and iced fruit at Grandma's house.
grammar: Buka puasa = breaking the fast at sunset; berbuka is the everyday verb.

target: Menjelang sore, pedagang takjil memenuhi trotoar di depan sekolah.
english: Toward late afternoon, takjil vendors fill the sidewalk in front of the school.
grammar: Takjil = small sweets and snacks for breaking the fast, sold roadside every afternoon.

target: Adik saya baru belajar puasa setengah hari tahun ini.
english: My little sibling is just learning to fast half a day this year.

target: Setelah buka puasa, ayah dan kakak pergi tarawih di masjid dekat rumah.
english: After breaking the fast, Dad and my older sibling go to tarawih prayers at the mosque near home.
grammar: Tarawih = the extra evening prayers at the mosque on Ramadan nights.

target: Ibu memasak kolak pisang untuk menu buka puasa hari pertama.
english: Mom cooks banana kolak for the first day's fast-breaking menu.

target: Jalan raya sangat sepi saat orang-orang sedang berbuka di rumah masing-masing.
english: The main road is very quiet while people are breaking the fast in their own homes.

target: Selama puasa, rapat kantor biasanya digeser ke pagi hari.
english: During the fasting month, office meetings are usually shifted to the morning.

target: Dia tetap kuat bekerja seharian meskipun sedang berpuasa.
english: He still has the strength to work all day even though he is fasting.

target: Suara bedug dari masjid menandakan waktu berbuka sudah tiba.
english: The sound of the mosque drum signals that the time to break the fast has arrived.

target: Kami sering diundang buka puasa bersama di rumah teman ayah.
english: We are often invited to a group iftar at the house of Dad's friend.

target: Anak-anak berlatih menahan lapar dan haus sampai sore hari.
english: The children practice holding back hunger and thirst until late afternoon.

target: Pasar sore dadakan muncul di dekat stasiun selama bulan puasa.
english: An impromptu afternoon market pops up near the station during the fasting month.

target: Minggu terakhir Ramadan, ibu mengajak kami mencari baju baru di pusat perbelanjaan.
english: In the last week of Ramadan, Mom takes us to look for new clothes at the mall.

target: Malam takbiran, suara takbir terdengar dari masjid sampai pagi.
english: On takbiran night, the sound of the takbir can be heard from the mosques until morning.
grammar: Malam takbiran = the eve of Lebaran; takbir chants echo from mosques all night.

target: Kantor kami mengadakan buka puasa bersama di restoran Padang.
english: Our office holds a group iftar at a Padang restaurant.

target: Banyak orang membayar zakat di masjid pada akhir Ramadan.
english: Many people pay their alms at the mosque at the end of Ramadan.

target: Dua hari sebelum Lebaran, kami mudik ke kampung halaman ayah di Jawa Tengah.
english: Two days before Lebaran, we travel home to Dad's hometown in Central Java.

target: Karyawan biasanya menerima THR paling lambat seminggu sebelum hari raya.
english: Employees usually receive their holiday bonus at the latest a week before the holiday.
grammar: THR = Tunjangan Hari Raya, the holiday bonus: one month's salary, required by law.

target: Adik langsung membeli sepatu baru begitu THR ayah cair.
english: My little sibling buys new shoes right away as soon as Dad's holiday bonus comes through.
grammar: Cair (lit. 'liquid') = paid out: THR cair — the money has landed.

target: Pagi hari raya, kami ikut salat Idulfitri di lapangan dekat rumah.
english: On the holiday morning, we join the Eid prayer at the field near the house.

target: Setelah salat, kami sungkeman kepada kakek dan nenek di ruang tamu.
english: After the prayer, we do the sungkeman to Grandpa and Grandma in the living room.
grammar: Sungkeman: kneeling before elders to ask forgiveness — the tearjerker of Lebaran morning.

target: Ibu menyiapkan ketupat, opor ayam, dan sambal goreng ati sejak subuh.
english: Mom prepares ketupat, chicken opor, and spicy fried liver from before dawn.

target: Ketupat buatan nenek selalu lebih padat daripada buatan kami.
english: Grandma's ketupat is always denser than the ones we make.
grammar: Ketupat: rice cakes boiled in woven palm-leaf pouches — Lebaran's signature food.

target: Kami berkeliling kompleks untuk bersilaturahmi dengan para tetangga.
english: We go around the complex to pay friendly visits to the neighbors.
grammar: Silaturahmi = keeping ties warm; bersilaturahmi is what all the visiting is called.

target: Anak-anak antre salaman sambil menerima amplop kecil dari om dan tante.
english: The kids line up to shake hands while receiving small envelopes from their uncles and aunts.

target: Toples nastar di meja tamu sudah setengah kosong sebelum siang.
english: The jar of nastar cookies on the guest table is already half empty before noon.

target: Kue kering buatan ibu selalu habis lebih dulu daripada yang dibeli di toko.
english: Mom's homemade cookies always run out sooner than the store-bought ones.

target: Kami mengucapkan mohon maaf lahir dan batin kepada semua saudara.
english: We say 'forgive me, outwardly and inwardly' to all our relatives.
grammar: Mohon maaf lahir dan batin ≈ 'forgive my wrongs, outward and inner' — the Lebaran formula.

target: Kantor kami mengadakan halal bihalal seminggu setelah libur Lebaran.
english: Our office holds a halal bihalal gathering a week after the Lebaran break.
grammar: Halal bihalal: a post-Lebaran gathering for mutual forgiveness, beloved by offices.

target: Acara halal bihalal keluarga besar tahun ini diadakan di rumah paman tertua.
english: This year's extended-family halal bihalal is held at the eldest uncle's house.

target: Menurut berita, arus balik tahun ini lebih padat daripada arus mudik.
english: According to the news, this year's return traffic is heavier than the outbound exodus.
grammar: Arus mudik = the outbound exodus; arus balik = the return wave. News-speak you'll hear daily.

target: Tiket kereta untuk mudik habis terjual dalam beberapa jam saja.
english: Train tickets for the homecoming sold out in just a few hours.

target: Nenek membagikan uang baru kepada semua cucunya setiap pagi Lebaran.
english: Grandma hands out crisp new banknotes to all her grandchildren every Lebaran morning.

target: Kami menukar uang lama dengan uang baru di bank sebelum mudik.
english: We exchange old bills for new ones at the bank before going home for the holiday.

target: Rumah kakek penuh dengan mobil saudara dari berbagai kota selama Lebaran.
english: Grandpa's house is full of relatives' cars from various cities during Lebaran.

target: Hari kedua Lebaran, keluarga besar berziarah ke makam kakek buyut.
english: On the second day of Lebaran, the extended family visits great-grandfather's grave.

target: Ibu memesan parsel berisi sirup dan kue untuk dikirim kepada tetangga lama.
english: Mom orders a hamper of syrup and cookies to be sent to an old neighbor.

target: Baju koko ayah masih bagus, tetapi dia tetap membeli satu lagi.
english: Dad's koko shirt is still in good shape, but he buys another one anyway.

target: Setiap Lebaran, berat badan saya naik karena opor dan rendang.
english: Every Lebaran my weight goes up because of the opor and rendang.

target: Grup keluarga penuh dengan kartu ucapan hari raya digital sejak subuh.
english: The family group chat has been full of digital holiday greeting cards since dawn.

target: Asisten rumah tangga kami pulang kampung, jadi rumah agak berantakan.
english: Our household helper has gone back to her village, so the house is a bit of a mess.

target: Jakarta terasa kosong saat semua orang merayakan Lebaran di kampung masing-masing.
english: Jakarta feels empty when everyone is celebrating Lebaran back in their own hometowns.

target: Saat Imlek, keluarga besar teman saya berkumpul untuk makan malam bersama.
english: At Chinese New Year, my friend's extended family gathers for dinner together.
grammar: Imlek = Chinese New Year — a public holiday in Indonesia since 2003.

target: Anak-anak yang belum menikah menerima angpao dari om dan tante mereka.
english: Children who are not yet married receive red envelopes from their uncles and aunts.
grammar: Angpao: red envelopes of cash at Imlek — married adults give, unmarried receive.

target: Kami mengajak anak-anak menonton pertunjukan barongsai di pusat perbelanjaan.
english: We take the kids to watch a lion dance performance at the shopping center.
grammar: Barongsai = the Chinese lion dance; malls book troupes all through Imlek.

target: Lampion merah digantung di sepanjang jalan menuju kelenteng tua itu.
english: Red lanterns are hung all along the road leading to the old Chinese temple.

target: Ibu teman saya membuat kue keranjang untuk dibagikan kepada para tetangga.
english: My friend's mother makes sticky rice cakes to hand out to the neighbors.
grammar: Kue keranjang: sticky sweet rice cake — Imlek's must-have, like ketupat at Lebaran.

target: Menurut teman saya, hujan saat Imlek dianggap membawa rezeki.
english: According to my friend, rain at Chinese New Year is considered to bring good fortune.

target: Toko kue itu menerima pesanan kue keranjang sejak sebulan sebelumnya.
english: That bakery takes orders for sticky rice cakes from a month beforehand.

target: Seluruh keluarga memakai baju berwarna merah saat makan malam Imlek.
english: The whole family wears red clothes at the Chinese New Year dinner.

target: Kantor teman saya tutup dua hari karena perayaan Imlek jatuh pada hari Senin.
english: My friend's office is closed for two days because Imlek falls on a Monday.

target: Dia mengucapkan selamat tahun baru Imlek kepada tetangganya sambil tersenyum.
english: She wishes her neighbor a happy Chinese New Year with a smile.

target: Keluarga tante saya menghias pohon Natal besar di ruang tamu mereka.
english: My aunt's family decorates a big Christmas tree in their living room.

target: Kami menghadiri ibadah malam Natal di gereja dekat rumah nenek.
english: We attend the Christmas Eve service at the church near Grandma's house.

target: Anak-anak membuka kado Natal mereka pagi-pagi sekali tanggal dua puluh lima.
english: The children open their Christmas presents very early on the twenty-fifth.

target: Ibu memasak ayam panggang khusus untuk makan malam Natal.
english: Mom cooks roast chicken specially for Christmas dinner.

target: Toko-toko memutar lagu Natal sejak awal bulan Desember.
english: The shops have been playing Christmas songs since the beginning of December.

target: Malam tahun baru, kami membakar jagung dan sate di halaman belakang.
english: On New Year's Eve, we grill corn and satay in the backyard.
grammar: Bakar jagung — grilling corn with the neighbors — is the default New Year's Eve plan.

target: Suara terompet kertas anak-anak ramai sekali menjelang tengah malam.
english: The sound of the children's paper horns gets really noisy toward midnight.

target: Kembang api menyala di langit kota tepat jam dua belas malam.
english: Fireworks light up the city sky exactly at twelve o'clock at night.
grammar: Spoken time uses jam: jam dua belas malam = 12 at night. Pukul is for announcements.

target: Kami menonton pesta kembang api dari atap gedung apartemen teman.
english: We watch the fireworks show from the roof of a friend's apartment building.

target: Jalan menuju Puncak macet total setiap malam tahun baru.
english: The road to Puncak is completely jammed every New Year's Eve.
grammar: Puncak = the mountain resort area south of Jakarta; macet total every long weekend.

target: Tahun ini resolusi saya lebih sederhana: tidur cukup dan olahraga teratur.
english: This year my resolution is simpler: enough sleep and regular exercise.

target: Kami begadang sampai pagi sambil main kartu dan makan jagung bakar.
english: We stay up till morning playing cards and eating grilled corn.

target: Beberapa keluarga memilih menginap di vila untuk menyambut tahun baru.
english: Some families choose to stay at a villa to welcome the new year.

target: Petasan berbunyi di mana-mana sampai bayi tetangga terbangun dan menangis.
english: Firecrackers go off everywhere until the neighbor's baby wakes up and cries.

target: Pagi tahun baru, jalanan penuh sampah sisa perayaan semalam.
english: On New Year's morning, the streets are full of trash left from last night's celebration.

target: Saat Nyepi, seluruh pulau Bali benar-benar sunyi selama satu hari penuh.
english: During Nyepi, the whole island of Bali goes completely silent for a full day.
grammar: Nyepi = Bali's Day of Silence: no lights, no travel, no work, for a full day.

target: Bandara di Bali tutup total selama Nyepi, jadi periksa jadwal penerbanganmu.
english: The airport in Bali closes completely during Nyepi, so check your flight schedule.
grammar: For Nyepi even the airport shuts — Bali's is the only one in the world that does.

target: Turis harus tetap berada di dalam hotel selama hari raya Nyepi.
english: Tourists must stay inside their hotels throughout the Nyepi holiday.

target: Malam sebelum Nyepi, pawai ogoh-ogoh memenuhi jalan-jalan di Denpasar.
english: The night before Nyepi, ogoh-ogoh parades fill the streets of Denpasar.
grammar: Ogoh-ogoh: giant demon figures paraded on Nyepi eve, then usually burned.

target: Anak-anak muda mengarak ogoh-ogoh raksasa buatan banjar mereka.
english: The young people parade the giant ogoh-ogoh built by their neighborhood association.

target: Kami memesan kamar hotel dengan makanan lengkap karena semua restoran tutup.
english: We book a hotel room with full meals because all the restaurants are closed.

target: Lampu-lampu di seluruh desa dimatikan, dan langit malam penuh bintang.
english: The lights across the whole village are turned off, and the night sky is full of stars.

target: Layanan internet di ponsel juga dimatikan selama hari Nyepi.
english: Mobile internet service is switched off as well during Nyepi day.
grammar: Since 2018 even mobile internet is off during Nyepi — download your maps early.

target: Sehari setelah Nyepi, warga saling berkunjung untuk bermaaf-maafan.
english: The day after Nyepi, residents visit one another to exchange apologies.

target: Sebelum Nyepi, umat Hindu melakukan upacara Melasti di pantai.
english: Before Nyepi, Hindu worshippers perform the Melasti ceremony on the beach.

target: Teman saya sengaja datang ke Bali untuk merasakan suasana Nyepi.
english: My friend comes to Bali on purpose to experience the atmosphere of Nyepi.

target: Hotel kami menyiapkan kegiatan meditasi dan yoga selama hari sunyi itu.
english: Our hotel prepares meditation and yoga activities during the day of silence.

target: Kami merencanakan pesta kejutan untuk ulang tahun ibu bulan depan.
english: We are planning a surprise party for Mom's birthday next month.

target: Semua tamu bersembunyi di ruang tamu sebelum ibu pulang kerja.
english: All the guests hide in the living room before Mom comes home from work.

target: Waktu lampu menyala, kami semua berteriak, dan ibu menangis terharu.
english: When the lights come on, we all shout, and Mom cries with emotion.

target: Sebelum meniup lilin, adik memejamkan mata dan mengucapkan harapan dalam hati.
english: Before blowing out the candles, my little sibling closes her eyes and makes a wish silently.
grammar: The tiup lilin ritual: close your eyes, make a wish, blow — and never tell the wish.

target: Tahun ini kakek meniup lilin angka delapan puluh dengan bantuan cucu-cucunya.
english: This year Grandpa blows out the number-eighty candle with his grandchildren's help.

target: Menurut kebiasaan kantor, yang berulang tahun wajib mentraktir teman-temannya.
english: By office custom, whoever has a birthday must treat their friends.
grammar: Birthday rule reversed: the birthday person treats everyone — dia yang mentraktir!

target: Teman-teman menaburkan tepung ke rambutnya setelah acara tiup lilin.
english: His friends sprinkle flour onto his hair after the candle-blowing.
grammar: Getting doused with flour (and eggs) on your birthday is an affectionate prank.

target: Sekretaris kantor memesan nasi tumpeng kuning untuk syukuran ulang tahun perusahaan.
english: The office secretary orders a yellow rice cone for the company's anniversary thanksgiving.
grammar: Tumpeng: a yellow rice cone for milestones; the first slice goes to the most honored guest.

target: Potongan tumpeng pertama diberikan kepada kakek sebagai tanda hormat.
english: The first slice of the tumpeng is given to Grandpa as a sign of respect.

target: Kami hanya merayakan ulang tahun anak dengan doa dan makan bersama.
english: We celebrate our child's birthday simply with a prayer and a meal together.

target: Kakak mengunggah foto masa kecil saya dengan ucapan panjang di media sosial.
english: My older sibling uploads my childhood photo with a long birthday message on social media.

target: Kado ulang tahun kakak dari ayah tahun ini tiket konser band favoritnya.
english: My older sibling's birthday present from Dad this year is a ticket to her favorite band's concert.

target: Keluarga kami mengadakan syukuran kecil setelah adik lulus kuliah.
english: Our family holds a small thanksgiving gathering after my younger sibling graduates from college.
grammar: Syukuran: a small thanksgiving meal for any good news — a degree, a house, a baby.

target: Tetangga mengundang kami ke syukuran rumah baru mereka besok malam.
english: The neighbors invite us to the housewarming blessing for their new house tomorrow night.

target: Sebelum pindah rumah, keluarga kami membagikan nasi kotak kepada para tetangga.
english: Before moving house, our family hands out boxed rice meals to the neighbors.

target: Acara tujuh bulanan kakak ipar dihadiri seluruh keluarga besar.
english: My sister-in-law's seventh-month pregnancy ceremony is attended by the whole extended family.
grammar: Tujuh bulanan: the blessing ceremony held in the seventh month of a pregnancy.

target: Di kampung ayah, panen besar juga dirayakan dengan makan bersama di sawah.
english: In Dad's village, a big harvest is also celebrated with a shared meal in the rice fields.

target: Kalender Indonesia penuh hari libur karena semua agama besar dirayakan.
english: The Indonesian calendar is full of holidays because all the major religions are celebrated.
grammar: Indonesia's calendar marks the holidays of six religions — everyone shares the days off.

target: Setiap perayaan di Indonesia hampir selalu berakhir dengan makan bersama keluarga.
english: Almost every celebration in Indonesia ends with a meal together with family.
